title: The Lost Puppy
description: Read the short story, then answer the questions below.
story:
One afternoon, Sara was walking home from school when she heard a small barking sound behind a tree. She looked and saw a tiny puppy shivering in the cold. The puppy had no collar and looked very hungry.

Sara gently picked up the puppy and took it home. She gave it some food and water. Later that evening, Sara and her father made posters to help find the puppy's owner.

The next day, a neighbor saw the poster and came to Sara's house. The puppy happily ran to the neighbor because it belonged to him. The neighbor thanked Sara for taking care of his puppy.

Sara felt happy because she helped someone in need.

title: NC Grade 3 — Numbers, Operations & Shapes
description: These questions are based on your NC Rethink Education worksheets. Read the Key Vocabulary first, then answer each question.
story:
KEY VOCABULARY (from your worksheet):

Place Value — The value of where a digit is in a number.
   Example: In 495 → 4 = Hundreds, 9 = Tens, 5 = Ones

Standard Form — Writing a number using digits.
   Example: two thousand forty = 2,040

Expanded Form — Breaking a number to show the value of each digit.
   Example: 356 = 300 + 50 + 6

Rounding — Changing a number to the nearest ten or hundred to make it simpler.
   Example: 79 rounds UP to 80. 34 rounds DOWN to 30.

Front-End Estimation — Estimate by keeping only the highest place value digit and making the rest zeros.
   Example: 458 → 400.   311 → 300.

Unknown Number — A missing number in an equation shown with a symbol (? or a letter).
   Example: 24 + ? = 83   or   A − 42 = 200

Inverse Operation — The opposite operation that undoes another.
   Addition ↔ Subtraction     Multiplication ↔ Division

2-Dimensional Shape — A flat shape with only length and width (no depth).

Polygon — A closed 2-D shape made of 3 or more straight sides with no curves and no crossing lines.

Attribute — A property of a shape, like the number of sides or angles.

Compose — To put parts or pieces together to make a shape.

title: Surah An-Naba — Reading & Memorization (Ayat 1–26)
description: Read Surah An-Naba from Ayah 1 to Ayah 26 with your parent. Then answer the questions. The last questions focus on memorizing Ayah 26 word by word.
story:
SURAH AN-NABA (The Great News) — Surah 78
Read aloud with your parent. Arabic → Transliteration → English meaning.

Ayah 1:  عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ
         Amma yatasaa-aloon
         About what are they asking one another?

Ayah 2:  عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ
         Anil naba-il azeem
         About the great news —

Ayah 3:  الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ
         Allathee hum feehi mukhtalifoon
         That over which they disagree.

Ayah 4:  كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ
         Kalla saya'lamoon
         No! They are going to know.

Ayah 5:  ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ
         Thumma kalla saya'lamoon
         Then, no! They are going to know.

Ayah 6:  أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا
         Alam naj'alil arda mihadaa
         Have We not made the earth a resting place?

Ayah 7:  وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا
         Wal jibala awtadaa
         And the mountains as stakes?

Ayah 8:  وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا
         Wa khalaqnakum azwajaa
         And We created you in pairs.

Ayah 9:  وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا
         Wa ja'alna nawmakum subataa
         And made your sleep a means of rest.

Ayah 10: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا
         Wa ja'alnal layla libasaa
         And made the night as clothing.

Ayah 11: وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا
         Wa ja'alnan nahara ma'ashaa
         And made the day for livelihood.

Ayah 12: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا
         Wa banayna fawqakum sab'an shidadaa
         And constructed above you seven strong heavens.

Ayah 13: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا
         Wa ja'alna sirajan wahajaa
         And made a blazing lamp (the sun).

Ayah 14: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا
         Wa anzalna minal mu'sirati ma-an thajjajaa
         And sent down from the rain clouds pouring water.

Ayah 15: لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا
         Linukhrija bihi habban wa nabataa
         That We may bring forth grain and vegetation.

Ayah 16: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا
         Wa jannatin alfafaa
         And gardens of entwined growth.

Ayah 17: إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا
         Inna yawmal fasli kana meqataa
         Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time.

Ayah 18: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا
         Yawma yunfakhu fis suri fata'toona afwajaa
         The Day the Horn is blown and you come forth in multitudes.

Ayah 19: وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا
         Wa futihatil sama-u fakanat abwabaa
         And the heaven is opened and becomes gateways.

Ayah 20: وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا
         Wa suyyiratil jibalu fakanat sarabaa
         And the mountains are removed and become a mirage.

Ayah 21: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا
         Inna jahannama kanat mirsadaa
         Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait —

Ayah 22: لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا
         Lil tagheena ma-abaa
         For the transgressors, a place of return.

Ayah 23: لَّابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا
         Labiteena feeha ahqabaa
         In which they will remain for ages unending.

Ayah 24: لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا
         La yathooqoona feeha bardan wa la sharabaa
         They will taste no coolness therein, nor any drink —

Ayah 25: إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا
         Illa hameeman wa ghassaqaa
         Except scalding water and foul purulence.

Ayah 26: جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا
         Jaza-an Wifaqaa
         A fitting recompense.

★ MEMORIZE AYAH 26 — WORD BY WORD ★
  This ayah has only TWO words:
  Word 1: جَزَاءً  →  Jaza-an  →  Means: A recompense (a reward or punishment)
  Word 2: وِفَاقًا  →  Wifaqaa  →  Means: Fitting / Appropriate
  Full ayah: Jaza-an Wifaqaa = A fitting recompense.
  Practice: Say Word 1 → say both words → close your eyes and say it alone.
